summary: An undergraduate computer science reader who has studied discrete mathematics, algorithms (divide and conquer, fast multiplication such as Karatsuba, the FFT at a basic level), linear algebra, and elementary number theory and probability. They know asymptotic notation, binary and positional number representation, polynomials and complex numbers, and basic Turing machines. They have not studied multitape complexity details, advanced harmonic analysis, algebraic number theory, or the research literature on integer multiplication.

known.name: Binary representation and radix digits
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of digits in a given base, with the leftmost digit most significant.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Integers are compared by their remainders on division by a modulus, and arithmetic is done on these remainders.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and integers with gcd 1 are coprime.

known.name: Logarithms and powers of two
known.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm, and ceiling and floor round up and down to integers.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and convolution of sequences
known.gloss: The product of two polynomials has coefficients given by sums of products of pairs of coefficients with indices adding to the given degree.

known.name: Karatsuba and divide-and-conquer multiplication
known.gloss: Recursively splitting operands into halves to multiply faster than the quadratic schoolbook method.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform basics
known.gloss: The standard O(N log N) algorithm for evaluating a sequence at the N-th roots of unity, using the primitive complex root of unity e^{2 pi i/N}.

known.name: Linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers
known.gloss: Vectors, matrices, linear maps, invertibility, subspaces and dimension.

known.name: Direct product of sets and multidimensional arrays
known.gloss: A multidimensional array is indexed by tuples of coordinates, one per axis, and stored linearly in some order.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of positions, which can be composed and inverted.

known.name: Cyclic groups and Z/mZ
known.gloss: Integers modulo m under addition, with indices wrapping around.

known.name: Fixed-point and rounding arithmetic
known.gloss: Numbers represented with a fixed number of bits after the point, with rounding errors bounded and tracked.

known.name: Error bounds and the triangle inequality
known.gloss: Magnitudes of sums are bounded by sums of magnitudes, and the maximum absolute value of coordinates measures a vector.

known.name: Binary XOR and bitwise operations
known.gloss: Bitwise operations on binary words, with XOR being addition mod 2 on each bit.

known.name: Basic counting and combinatorics
known.gloss: Counting subsets and intersections of finite sets.

known.name: Induction and recurrences
known.gloss: Proving statements recursively and solving recurrences for running time.

known.name: Real analysis basics: inequalities and exponentials
known.gloss: Standard facts about exp, sine, cosine, and bounding sums by integrals.

known.name: Ring and group axioms
known.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication satisfying standard laws, as met in discrete mathematics.
